args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the latest deploy of checkout-api v2.3.1 (all regions: us-east, us-west, eu-west), the service failed health checks with an error rate of ~18%. v2.3.1 was also unhealthy in staging (v2.3.1-rc). Action taken: rolled checkout-api back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. Post-rollback status: healthy, error rate ~0.2%. Follow-up: investigate the v2.3.1 regression before redeploying, and review why an RC that was unhealthy in staging got promoted to production.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened the SEV2 incident.

- **What was wrong:** v2.3.1 was running in all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west). It was failing health checks with an error rate of about 18%.
- **Rollback:** The deploy history shows v2.3.0 as the most recent release that was healthy in production, so that's the version I rolled back to. After the rollback, all three regions run v2.3.0, the service passes health checks and the error rate is down to about 0.2%.
- **Incident:** The SEV2 incident is titled "checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0". It describes the failure, the rollback and the recovered numbers. Opening it paged the on-call engineer. A human operator confirmed it went through, so I didn't open a second one.

The release candidate for v2.3.1 was already failing health checks in staging before it went to production. The incident lists two follow-ups: find out why v2.3.1 is broken before redeploying it, and why a release that failed in staging was still pushed to production.
